He is the vice president of basketball development for the [[Miami Heat]], where he [[List of NBA players who have spent their entire career with one franchise|spent his entire 20-year playing career]] in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Haslem is one of only three players in NBA history to play at least 20 years with one team.{{Cite web |last=Issa |first=Mat |title=Udonis Haslem Continues To Show Why He's 'The Mayor Of Miami' |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/matissa/2024/09/20/udonis-haslem-continues-to-show-why-hes-the-mayor-of-miami/ |access-date=2024-09-24 |website=Forbes |language=en}} He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]], where he was a key member of four [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] teams. Haslem began his professional career in France with [[Élan Chalon|Chalon-sur-Saône]] and then signed with his hometown team, the Miami Heat, in 2003, leaving as the longest-tenured player in franchise history when he retired 20 years later. Haslem won three [[NBA Finals|NBA championships]] in [[2006 NBA Finals|2006]], [[2012 NBA Finals|2012]] and [[2013 NBA Finals|2013]]. ==Early life== Haslem was born in [[Miami]]. His father, John, played college basketball for the [[Stetson Hatters men's basketball|Stetson Hatters]] from 1972 to 1974.{{cite web |last=Joseph |first=Dave |title=Mom's the Word |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/fl-xpm-2005-04-26-0504260050-story.html |website=South Florida Sun Sentinel |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=April 26, 2005}}{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball Record Book |url=https://static.gohatters.com/custompages/pdf/Stetson_MBB_Record_Book.pdf |website=Stetson University |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=July 14, 2020}} His mother, Debra, was Puerto Rican.{{cite news |author=Heyes |first=Mark |date=September 3, 2013 |title=Miami Heat Player Udonis Haslem's Wedding Story Is Strange And Beautiful |publisher=[[BuzzFeed]] |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/mikehayes/miami-heat-player-udonis-haslems-wedding-story-is-strange-an |url-status=live |access-date=May 7, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130906051325/http://www.buzzfeed.com/mikehayes/miami-heat-player-udonis-haslems-wedding-story-is-strange-an |archive-date=September 6, 2013}} Haslem attended [[Samuel W. Wolfson High School|Wolfson High School]] in [[Jacksonville, Florida]], then [[Miami High School|Miami Senior High School]] in Miami.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoopshype.com/players/udonis_haslem.htm |title=NBA Players – Udonis Haslem |publisher=Hoops Hype |access-date=October 5, 2007 |archive-date=November 26, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131126034541/http://www.hoopshype.com/players/udonis_haslem.htm }} He helped lead Miami High to state titles in 1997 and 1998 (the last two of three in a row), playing alongside another future NBA player, [[Steve Blake]]. The team was coached by UMass Amherst head coach [[Frank Martin (basketball)|Frank Martin]]. However, an investigation by the ''[[Miami New Times]]'' revealed that Haslem, Blake and several other players circumvented residency requirements. The ''New Times'' reported that while he claimed to live in Miami, Haslem lived in [[Miramar, Florida|Miramar]]. His official school address was an efficiency apartment owned by a longtime Miami High [[Booster club|booster]], which was also a violation of [[Florida High School Athletic Association]] (FHSAA) rules.{{cite news|last=Powell |first=Robert Andrew |url=http://www.miaminewtimes.com/1998-03-05/news/dream-team |title=Dream Team |newspaper=[[Miami New Times]] |date=March 5, 1998 |access-date=April 3, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140108072208/http://www.miaminewtimes.com/1998-03-05/news/dream-team |archive-date=January 8, 2014 |url-status=live }}{{cite news|last=Powell |first=Robert Andrew |url=http://www.miaminewtimes.com/1998-07-02/news/double-dribbling |title=Double Dribbling |newspaper=Miami New Times |date=July 2, 1998 |access-date=April 3, 2011 |archive-date=January 8, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140108060923/http://www.miaminewtimes.com/1998-07-02/news/double-dribbling |url-status=live }} As a result, Miami High was stripped of its 1998 title and ordered to forfeit its entire schedule. ==College career== Haslem accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in [[Gainesville, Florida]], where he played for coach [[Billy Donovan]]'s [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Gators]] teams from 1998 to 2002 while majoring in leisure service management. As the Gators' starting [[center (basketball)|center]] for four years, Haslem was part of Donovan's 1998 recruiting class that raised the national prominence of the Florida Gators basketball program and included future Miami Heat teammate [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]]. Haslem's sophomore season saw the team advance to the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division I men's basketball championship]] game before falling to [[1999–2000 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] 89–76. The Gators received NCAA tournament invitations four consecutive years during Haslem's college career—the first time in the program's history. During his tenure with Florida, Haslem averaged 13.7 points per game and 6.7 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/udonis-haslem-1.html|title=Udonis Haslem|website=sports-reference.com|access-date=August 8, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005132119/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/udonis-haslem-1.html|archive-date=October 5, 2016}} He was named to the coaches' All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) team four times: as the third team in 1999 and 2000, and the first team in 2001 and 2002.{{cite web |title=2019–2020 Media Guide |url=https://floridagators.com/documents/2019/9/24//2019_20_Media_Guide.pdf?id=28811 |website=University of Florida |access-date=July 28, 2020 |date=September 24, 2019}} Haslem also ranks third in team history in points scored (1,782) and tenth in rebounds (831). He was inducted into the [[University of Florida Athletic Hall of Fame]] as a "Gator Great" in 2012.F Club, Hall of Fame, [http://www.gatorfclub.org/hall-of-fame/greats Gator Greats]. Retrieved December 13, 2014.{{cite news |access-date=September 24, 2011 |url=http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=21249 |title=Florida Announces 2012 UF Athletic Hall of Fame Inductees |publisher=GatorZone |date=September 7, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019081452/http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=21249 |archive-date=October 19, 2013 |url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Chalon-Sur-Saône (2002–2003)=== Haslem went undrafted in the [[2002 NBA draft]] primarily due to his relative lack of size for a forward as he measured just {{height|ft=6|in=6}} at the NBA pre-draft camp.{{cite web |last=Tomlinson |first=Dylan B. |title=Haslem invited to camp |url=https://www.gainesville.com/article/LK/20020709/News/604173091/GS |website=The Gainesville Sun |access-date=July 28, 2020 |date=July 9, 2002 |archive-date=January 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116183113/https://www.gainesville.com/article/LK/20020709/News/604173091/GS |url-status=dead }} [[Seattle SuperSonics]] coach [[Nate McMillan]] had promised to draft Haslem if he was still available in the second round, but the offer fell through.{{cite AV media | date=January 16, 2024 | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z5ZO_VHE6Mw | title=Jersey Retirement Special: UD Calls Out NBA GMs & Apologizes To Bill Russell's Family | time=12:29 | via=YouTube }} Haslem accepted an offer to join the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for training camp and made their roster for the [[Reebok Pro Summer League|Shaw's Pro Summer League]].{{cite web |title=Celtics host Shaw's Pro Summer League |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/s/2002/0716/1406550.html |website=ESPN |access-date=July 28, 2020 |date=July 18, 2002}} However, he was released by the Hawks before the start of the [[2002–03 NBA season]].{{cite web |last=Goodman |first=Joseph |title=Udonis Haslem takes unusual route to become Miami Heat's rebounding leader |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/latest-news/article1944809.html |website=Miami Herald |access-date=July 28, 2020 |date=November 23, 2012}} Haslem signed with [[Élan Chalon|Chalon-Sur-Saône]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]]. He arrived in France weighing nearly {{convert|300|lb}}. While in France, Haslem lost {{convert|50|lb}} in eight months.{{cite news|last=Haberstroh |first=Tom |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/miamiheat/post/_/id/15951 |title=Udonis Haslem: Unlikely rebounding story |work=ESPN.com |date=November 21, 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130523183019/http://espn.go.com/blog/truehoop/miamiheat/post/_/id/15951/udonis-haslem-a-rebounding-story |archive-date=May 23, 2013|access-date=August 6, 2026}} He averaged 16.1 points and 9.4 rebounds per game in his lone season with the team. ===Miami Heat (2003–2023)=== ====2003–08: All-Rookie honors and first championship==== [[File:UdonisHaslem.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Haslem in 2007]] On August 6, 2003, Haslem signed with his hometown team, the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web |last=Bryant |first=L |date=August 6, 2003 |title=HEAT Sign Free Agent Forward Udonis Haslem |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_sign_haslem_030806.html |access-date=May 2, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} As a rookie, Haslem played in the Rookie Challenge during All-Star weekend, earned [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] honors, and helped the Heat reach the Eastern Conference Semifinals.{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIA/2004_games.html |title=2003-04 Miami Heat Schedule and Results |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2019-08-06}} In 2004–05, Haslem started in all 80 games in which he appeared, averaging 10.9 points, a career-high 9.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 33.4 minutes per game. Haslem's .540 field goal percentage ranked fifth on the Heat's all-time single-season list then and fourth in the NBA. He appeared in Rookie Challenge for the second straight year, this time for the sophomore team.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_resign_haslem_050802.html|title=HEAT Re-Sign Udonis Haslem|work=NBA.com|date=August 2, 2005|access-date=September 10, 2018}} Haslem re-signed with the Heat in August 2005. In June 2006, he helped the Heat win their first NBA Championship in six games over the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in the [[2006 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. Haslem recorded 17 points and 10 rebounds in the title-clinching Game 6.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hasleud01/gamelog/2006/|title=Udonis Haslem 2005-06 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=September 10, 2018}} Haslem scored a career-high 28 points on November 10, 2006, in a 113–106 victory over the [[New Jersey Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/261110017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911114517/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/261110017 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 11, 2018 |title=Shaq comes back to Heat but Wade burns Nets in win|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2006|access-date=March 27, 2020}} Since the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], Haslem was the team captain for the Heat.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/bio/udonis-haslem|title=Bio: Udonis Haslem|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 24, 2023}} On January 29, 2008, Haslem—who had been the only Miami player to start all 43 games of the 2007–08 season—suffered a sprained ankle during a 117–87 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/280129014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911114445/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/280129014|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 11, 2018|title=Powe, Rondo answer call for Celtics; Heat's Wade, Haslem leave game|work=ESPN.com|date=January 29, 2008|access-date=March 27, 2020}} He returned to action on February 23, only to play in five games before being ruled out for the rest of the season after reaggravating the ankle injury on March 7 against the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hasleud01/gamelog/2008/|title=Udonis Haslem 2007-08 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=September 10, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/280307014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911114438/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/280307014|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 11, 2018|title=Jackson scores 22 for Warriors, who hand Heat largest defeat of season|work=ESPN.com|date=March 7, 2008|access-date=September 10, 2018}} Haslem averaged a career-high 12.0 points per game in 2007–08. ====2009–13: Back-to-back championships==== In July 2010, Haslem signed a five-year deal worth approximately $20 million to remain with the Heat. The contract paid him roughly $14 million less than Haslem could have received if he accepted more lucrative offers from the [[Dallas Mavericks]] or [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/07/13/sports/basketball/13hoops.html|title=Haslem Takes Less Money to Stay With the Heat|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=July 12, 2010|access-date=September 10, 2018|agency=The Associated Press}} Haslem continued on with a new-look Heat roster that included [[LeBron James]] and [[Chris Bosh]] teaming up with [[Dwyane Wade]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5374210|title=Haslem stays with Heat; Miller joins in|work=ESPN.com|date=July 12, 2010|access-date=September 10, 2018}} In November 2010, Haslem sustained a torn ligament in his foot,{{cite web |date=November 24, 2010 |title=Udonis Haslem's season might be over |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/truehoop/miamiheat/news/story?id=5843177 |access-date=May 2, 2023 |work=ESPN.com}} which sidelined him for the rest of the regular season.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hasleud01/gamelog/2011/|title=Udonis Haslem 2010-11 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=September 10, 2018}} Haslem returned to action in May 2011 during the playoffs. That June, the Heat were defeated in six games by the Mavericks during the [[2011 NBA Finals]]. Haslem helped the Heat return to the [[2012 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] in 2012, where they defeated the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in five games with Haslem winning his second championship.{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIA/2012_games.html |title=2011-12 Miami Heat Schedule and Results |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2019-08-06}} In November 2012, Haslem passed [[Alonzo Mourning]] to become the franchise leader in total rebounds with 4,808, breaking Mourning's previous record of 4,807. Haslem also became the first undrafted player to lead an NBA franchise in rebounding.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8661728 |title=Udonis Haslem sets franchise record |work=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 21, 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203044039/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/8661728/udonis-haslem-miami-heat-breaks-alonzo-mourning-all-time-franchise-rebounding-record |archive-date=December 3, 2013}} In June 2013, Haslem won his third championship after the Heat defeated the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in seven games in the [[2013 NBA Finals]]. After the NBA Finals, Haslem revealed that he had played through much of the second half of the [[2012–13 Miami Heat season|2012–13 season]] with a torn right meniscus.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/heat/2013/06/29/udonis-haslem-miami-heat-surgery-knee-meniscus-injury/2476241/|title=Heat's Udonis Haslem played with injury, needs surgery|work=usatoday.com|date=June 29, 2013|access-date=September 10, 2018}} ====2013–23: "Player-coach" role and retirement==== In [[2013–14 Miami Heat season|2013–14]], Haslem lost the rotation spot that he had long occupied, and his on-court time continued to diminish significantly as the season progressed. Haslem played in just seven games in January and February combined, and played only two total minutes from January 21 to February 27.{{cite web|last=Richmond|first=Sam|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2021947-why-miami-heat-need-vintage-udonis-haslem-in-2014-playoffs|title=Why Miami Heat Need Vintage Udonis Haslem in 2014 Playoffs|work=bleacherreport.com|date=April 9, 2014|access-date=September 10, 2018}} He played in just 46 regular season games in 2013–14, averaging 3.8 points and 3.8 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.rappler.com/sports/63771-udonis-haslem-resigns-miami-heat/|title=Udonis Haslem re-signs with Miami Heat|work=Rappler.com|date=July 18, 2014|access-date=September 10, 2018}} The Heat returned to the [[2014 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] in 2014 for the fourth straight year, where they were defeated in five games by the Spurs. Following the 2013–14 season, Haslem decided to opt out of the final year of his contract.{{Cite news |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |authorlink=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=June 28, 2014 |title=Dwyane Wade, Chris Bosh, Udonis Haslem entering free agency in hope of keeping LeBron James in Miami |work=Yahoo.com |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/dwyane-wade--chris-bosh--udonis-haslem-entering-free-agency-in-hope-of-keeping-lebron-james-in-miami-173919540.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140701171347/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/dwyane-wade--chris-bosh--udonis-haslem-entering-free-agency-in-hope-of-keeping-lebron-james-in-miami-173919540.html |archive-date=July 1, 2014}} Haslem re-signed with the Heat on a two-year deal in July 2014.{{cite web |last=Herrera |first=Irene |date=July 18, 2014 |title=HEAT Re-Signs Udonis Haslem |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/heat-re-signs-udonis-haslem |access-date=May 2, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} At this point of his career, Haslem transitioned into a role that he and the organization described as a "player-coach", in that he rarely played on court but was more of a mentor to the younger players and assisted in their coaching. Haslem re-signed with the Heat on one-year deals in 2016,{{cite web |last=Herrera |first=Irene |date=July 10, 2016 |title=HEAT Re-Signs Udonis Haslem |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-udonis-haslem |access-date=May 2, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} 2017,{{cite web |last=Herrera |first=Irene |date=July 20, 2017 |title=HEAT Re-Signs Udonis Haslem |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-udonis-haslem-0 |access-date=May 2, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} and 2018.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-udonis-haslem-1|title=HEAT Re-Signs Udonis Haslem|work=NBA.com|date=September 10, 2018|access-date=September 10, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |title=Miami Heat re-sign Udonis Haslem |url=https://www.nba.com/news/miami-heat-re-sign-udonis-haslem |website=NBA.com |publisher=The Associated Press |access-date=November 29, 2020 |date=September 10, 2018}} In January 2019, Haslem indicated that the [[2018–19 Miami Heat season|2018–19 season]] would be his last.{{cite web|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|url=https://www.basketballinsiders.com/nba-daily-end-of-the-road-for-udonis-haslem/|title=NBA Daily: End of the Road for Udonis Haslem|work=basketballinsiders.com|date=January 2, 2019|access-date=March 8, 2019}}{{cite web |last=Chiang |first=Anthony |title=The Heat's Udonis Haslem reaffirms his plan to retire at end of season |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article224037165.html |website=Miami Herald |access-date=April 10, 2019 |date=January 7, 2019}} However, a few months later, Haslem stated that he had not decided if he was retiring and the decision would not be made until the [[2019–20 Miami Heat season|2019–20 season]].{{cite web |last=Winderman |first=Ira |title=Heat's Udonis Haslem says he will need time for retirement decision |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-udonis-halsem-s20190411-story.html |website=Sun-Sentinel.com |access-date=April 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412100300/https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-udonis-halsem-s20190411-story.html |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} On August 6, 2019, Haslem re-signed with the Heat on a one-year contract.{{cite web |last=Pendas |first=Christopher |date=August 6, 2019 |title=HEAT Re-Signs Udonis Haslem |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-haslem-20190806 |access-date=August 7, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}{{cite web |title='HeatLifer' Haslem, 39, returns for 17th season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27334860 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=August 7, 2019 |date=March 27, 2020}} During the 2019–20 season, he played in four games,{{cite web |title=Udonis Haslem 2019-20 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hasleud01/gamelog/2020 |website=basketball-reference.com |access-date=October 21, 2021}} including starting at power forward in a 109–92 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]] during the regular-season finale.{{cite web |title=Heat's Derrick Jones Jr. injured in 109-92 loss to Pacers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401224791 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=October 22, 2021 |date=August 14, 2021}} During that season, Haslem became the 30th player in league history to play after turning 40 years old,{{cite web |title=Oldest active NBA player entering 2021-22 and in league history |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/oldest-active-nba-player-entering-2021-22-and-league-history |website=NBC Sports |access-date=October 20, 2021 |date=October 7, 2021}} as well as the first modern era undrafted player to play to that age.{{citation needed|date=October 2020}} Following [[Vince Carter]]'s retirement during the [[2020 NBA Bubble|suspension of the season]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Haslem became the [[List of oldest and youngest National Basketball Association players|oldest active player in the NBA]]. The Heat reached the [[2020 NBA Finals]], losing in six games to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]; Haslem was on the active roster but did not play in the postseason. On November 28, 2020, Haslem re-signed with the Heat.{{cite web |title=The Captain Returns For His 18th Season |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/haslem-re-signs-with-heat-112820 |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 29, 2020 |date=November 28, 2020}}{{cite web |last=Chiang |first=Anthony |title=Pat Riley on Adebayo's extension, Haslem's return. And a look at NBA's health protocols |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article247476085.html |website=Miami Herald |access-date=November 29, 2020 |date=November 28, 2020}} He played in one game in the [[2020–21 Miami Heat season|2020–21 season]], on May 13, 2021, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Haslem scored four points in two minutes off the bench before getting ejected as a result of a scuffle with [[Dwight Howard]], making the 40-year-old Haslem the oldest player in the last 20 years to get ejected.{{cite web |title=Heat stay No. 5 in the East, roll past 76ers 106-94 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401307860 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=May 16, 2021 |date=May 13, 2021}} On August 15, 2021, Haslem re-signed with the Heat.{{cite web |title=HEAT Re-Signs Udonis Haslem |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-resigns-udonis-haslem-081621|last=Moorhead |first=Couper |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 23, 2021 |date=August 15, 2021}} On August 23, 2022, Haslem announced his intentions to retire after the [[2022–23 Miami Heat season|2022–23 season]], re-signing with the Heat for another year.{{cite web |title=Heat re-sign Udonis Haslem |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-sign-udonis-haslem-2 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=August 23, 2022}}{{cite web |last=Wimbish |first=Jasmyn |title=Heat veteran Udonis Haslem to return for historic 20th and final NBA season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/heat-veteran-udonis-haslem-to-return-for-historic-20th-and-final-nba-season/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=January 24, 2023 |date=August 22, 2022}} In his final regular season game on April 9, 2023, Haslem scored 24 points in 25 minutes during a 123–110 victory over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web |last=Friedell |first=Nick |title=Udonis Haslem scores 24 as Heat celebrate farewell game |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36134437 |website=ESPN.com |date=April 9, 2023 |access-date=April 9, 2023}} He became the second 42-year-old in NBA history to score 24 or more points in a game after [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] did so in Game 3 of the [[1989 NBA Finals]] and it marked Haslem's highest-scoring output since 2009.{{cite web |title=Haslem scores 24 in farewell, Heat top Magic 123-110 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401469374 |website=[[ESPN]] |date=April 9, 2023 |access-date=April 10, 2023}} His three [[three-point shot]]s in the game was a career high.{{cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-orlando-magic-20230409-qhotnl5ghrg2lnsgp3mkempyue-story.html|title=Heat hail Haslem in 123-110 win over Magic, with play-in showdown next against Hawks|accessdate=April 10, 2023|date=April 9, 2023|work=[[South Florida Sun Sentinel]]|last=Winderman |first=Ira}} At the age 42 years and 363 days, Haslem became the oldest person to play in the NBA Finals when he entered the fourth quarter of Game 3 of the [[2023 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] with 29.8 seconds remaining, breaking the mark of 42 years, 58 days set by [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] in 1989.{{cite magazine |last1=Neumann |first1=Thomas |title=Udonis Haslem Becomes Oldest Player to Appear in NBA Finals |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/06/08/udonis-haslem-oldest-player-appear-nba-finals |magazine=Sports Illustrated |access-date=June 15, 2023 |date=June 8, 2023}} After the Heat lost the NBA Finals to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in five games,{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Reynolds|title=Nuggets take home 1st NBA title in rugged 94–89 win over Heat|date=June 12, 2023|publisher=The Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401544850|access-date=June 13, 2023}} Haslem officially announced his retirement on July 28, 2023.{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/heat/2023/07/28/heats-udonis-haslem-announces-retirement-20-seasons/70488015007/ |title=Udonis Haslem, NBA's oldest player, retires from Heat after 20 seasons |first=Mike |last=Brehm |newspaper=USA Today |date=July 28, 2023 |access-date=August 9, 2023}} The Heat retired Haslem's {{abbr|No.|Number}} 40 jersey on January 19, 2024.{{cite web |last1=Reynolds |first1=Tim |title=Heat retire Udonis Haslem's No. 40 jersey |url=https://www.nba.com/news/heat-retire-udonis-haslem-40-jersey |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 20, 2024 |date=January 19, 2024}} ==Post-playing career== On November 8, 2023, the Heat hired Haslem to hold the role of vice president of basketball development.{{Cite web|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|url=https://www.nba.com/news/heat-sign-udonis-haslem-as-teams-vice-president|title=Heat add former big man Udonis Haslem to front office|agency=Associated Press|website=NBA.com|date=November 8, 2023|access-date=November 24, 2023}} In 2024, he began working as a television analyst, appearing on [[NBA TV]]'s postseason panel.{{cite news |last1=Chiang |first1=Anthony |title=Haslem's playing career is over, but he's still making presence felt for Heat during playoffs |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article288101120.html |access-date=20 June 2024 |work=[[Miami Herald]] |publisher=[[McClatchy]] |date=April 29, 2024}} Haslem has also made appearances for ESPN.{{cite news |last1=Jackson |first1=Barry |title=Heat's Haslem, wearing TV hat, offers idea for Herro and says what needs team must fill |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article288243545.html |access-date=20 June 2024 |work=[[Miami Herald]] |publisher=[[McClatchy]] |date=May 2, 2024}} Haslem joined [[NBA on Prime Video|Prime Video]] as a studio analyst during the [[2025–26 NBA season]].{{Cite web|url=https://press.amazonmgmstudios.com/us/en/press-release/prime-video-welcomes-udonis-haslem-steve-nash-cand|website=amazonmgmstudios.com |title=Prime Video Welcomes Udonis Haslem, Steve Nash, Candace Parker, and Dwyane Wade to NBA on Prime Team |date=May 5, 2025|access-date=August 6, 2026}} ==Other appearances== Haslem appeared in the music video for the song "[[G.D.F.R.]]" by [[Flo Rida]], as well as the music video for "Bet That" by [[Trick Daddy]], and the music video for [[Born-N-Raised]] by [[DJ Khaled]], [[Pitbull (rapper)|Pitbull]], Trick Daddy and [[Rick Ross]].{{citation needed|date=November 2020}} ==Personal life== [[File:Heat party.jpg|thumb|Haslem at a party with [[Dwyane Wade]] (center) and [[Antoine Walker]] (far right) in December 2005.]] Haslem is married to Faith Rein-Haslem, a sports broadcaster he dated for 14 years.{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/09/01/fashion/weddings/taking-their-very-sweet-time.html |title=Taking Their Very Sweet Time |last=Marx |first=Linda |date=2013-08-30 |website=The New York Times |access-date=2019-08-06}} They met in 1999 while attending the [[University of Florida]], where she was a member of the [[Florida Gators track and field]] team.{{Cite web |url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/Athlete.aspx?AID=7803370 |title=Faith Rein |website=Athletic.net |access-date=2019-08-06}} They have three sons. Haslem also has two brothers and three sisters.{{cite web |title=Udonis Haslem - NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/player/2617/udonis-haslem/rotowire |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 1, 2021}} After retirement, Haslem engaged in countless acts of philanthropy under the umbrella of his organization: the Udonis Haslem Children’s Foundation (UD Kids).{{Cite web |title=The Udonis Haslem Foundation - About Us |url=https://www.udcares.org/about-us |access-date=2024-09-24 |website=www.udcares.org}} He also partnered up with Wells Fargo to help repair homes in his area.{{Cite web |last=Issa |first=Mat |date=September 20, 2024 |title=Udonis Haslem Continues To Show Why He's 'The Mayor Of Miami' |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/matissa/2024/09/20/udonis-haslem-continues-to-show-why-hes-the-mayor-of-miami/ |access-date=2024-09-24 |website=Forbes |language=en}} Haslem, among other high-profile athletes and celebrities, was a paid spokesperson for [[FTX]], a [[cryptocurrency exchange]]. In November 2022, [[Bankruptcy of FTX|FTX filed for bankruptcy]] and wiped out billions of dollars in customer funds. Haslem, alongside other spokespeople, was sued for promoting unregistered securities through a [[Class action|class-action lawsuit]].{{cite news|last1=Zeitchik|first1=Steven|last2=Mark|first2=Julian|date=December 14, 2022|title=Tom Brady pushed crypto to his fans. This lawyer wants him to pay up.|newspaper=The Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2022/12/14/ftx-class-action-lawsuit/|access-date=December 14, 2022}}{{cite news|last=Anderson|first=Travis|date=November 16, 2022|title=Tom Brady, David Ortiz among athletes sued over crypto losses in federal lawsuit filed by investor|work=The Boston Globe|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2022/11/16/metro/tom-brady-david-ortiz-among-athletes-sued-over-crypto-losses-federal-lawsuit-filed-by-investor/|access-date=December 13, 2022}} In February 2022, the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit|U.S. 11th Circuit Court of Appeals]] ruled in a lawsuit against [[Bitconnect]] that the [[Securities Act of 1933]] extends to [[Targeted advertising|targeted solicitation]] using [[Influencer marketing|social media]].{{cite news|last=Lawler|first=Richard|date=February 18, 2022|title=Influencers beware: promoting the wrong crypto could mean facing a class-action lawsuit|website=The Verge|publisher=Vox Media|url=https://www.theverge.com/2022/2/18/22941470/bitconnect-ponzi-bitcoin-securities-act-sec-lawsuit-influencers-youtube-tiktok|access-date=July 13, 2022}} Haslem settled the FTX case, agreeing to pay an undisclosed amount.{{cite news |last=Horney |first=Ben |title=Udonis Haslem Settles Out of FTX Litigation |url=https://frontofficesports.com/udonis-haslem-settles-out-of-ftx-litigation/ |work=Front Office Sports |date=1 December 2025}} He purchased a minority stake in [[Ipswich Town F.C.]] in September of 2025, which was publicly announced in August 2026. {{cite news |last=Haslem|first=Udonis |title=Udonis Haslem purchases minority stake of Ipswich Town F.C. |url=https://x.com/ThisIsUD/status/2085422774814724592 |work=X |date=7 August 2026}} ==Career statistics==
